Exams and results

Result cards that agree with the marksheet

Marks go in once, per paper, by the teacher who marked them. Everything printed afterwards, the card, the tabulation sheet, the positions, is computed from that one set of numbers, so the three cannot disagree.

Start 14 day free trial Ask about your grading scale

The details that decide whether a card is right

Any software can average some numbers. These are the cases that produce a card a parent can argue with.

A paper not sat is not a zero

A pupil who was absent for one paper and a pupil whose marks have not been entered yet are different situations, and treating either as zero produces a card that is wrong. Both are tracked as what they are, and a card with a paper still outstanding says PROVISIONAL on it.

Practicals kept apart from theory

A practical is marked out of its own maximum, shown separately on the card, and combined with the theory for the pass mark. A subject that has no practical component cannot be given practical marks at all, so the two columns cannot quietly disagree.

Streams: nobody is marked out of the wrong syllabus

Where a class splits into streams, an Arts pupil is not marked against the Science papers and vice versa. The denominator for each pupil is the papers that pupil was actually meant to sit.

Your grading scale, and term weightage

Bands and grade points are yours to set, including a 10 point GPA if that is what your board uses. Term weightage is a setting too: if the final carries 70 per cent, the session mark carries the other 30 and the card says so.

Not built, and worth saying: credit weighted GPA. Every paper counts as one credit. A school running unequal credit hours gets an unweighted mean, which for almost every Pakistani school is the same number.

Results are released when you say so

Marks being entered is not the same as results being published. A card is not visible to a parent until it is released, so a teacher can enter marks on Tuesday and the school can hold them until Friday.

A result can also be withheld for one pupil, which every school occasionally needs and few systems allow without deleting something. And a correction after release is a new version with the change recorded, not a quiet edit: one message per child per term, so a fix does not spam forty parents.
